criteria.text: Determine whether the skill-injection preface (buildSkillsPreface / isSkillInjectionEnabled path in skill_retrieval.ts, called from the agent prompt assembly) filters candidate skills by the per-turn resolved agent profile's allowed_skills_json.
criteria.reason: Investigation outcome (documented in docs/ai/decisions/2026-06-28-skill-scope-enforcement.md): buildSkillsPreface DOES filter, but it operates on the api_server DB-skill store and is effectively inert for real enforcement. The skills the model actually sees/loads come from the opencode FORK (the `skill` tool + system-prompt listing of filesystem SKILL.md files). allowed_skills_json holds FORK skill names, so the real gap is fork-side: the fork never received the allowlist and served every discovered skill — the #765 shape.

criteria.text: If it does not, decide intended behavior: instance-wide shared (dead schema -> document/remove) OR per-agent scoped (parallel to MCP) -> implement enforcement at the injection site using the same per-turn agent resolution ws_gateway uses for MCP scope (perTurnAgent ?? agentKind).
criteria.test_id: issue-775-c4..c5 (filterSkillsByAllowlist / isSkillAllowed): per-agent scoped, mirroring mcpAllowlist — added a per-session fork skillAllowlist, filtered the two prompt seams + skill tool execute, and pushed it from ws_gateway/agent_runner via the same perTurnAgent ?? agentKind resolution.

criteria.text: Add a runtime regression guard mirroring tools/release/smoke_mcp_allowlist.sh — assert that an agent with a restricted allowed_skills_json does not get out-of-scope skills injected. (The #765 lesson: a guard that runs the real path, not a mock.)
criteria.test_id: tools/release/smoke_skill_allowlist.sh — boots the REAL built opencode binary, PATCHes a per-session skillAllowlist, and asserts it round-trips on GET (null/absent on an unpatched binary). Wired into desktop_release.yml as the #775 guard.
